name: SplitButton
purpose: Lets people perform a primary action, or choose from a small group of similar actions via an attached Dropdown Menu.
intent: A thin composition of Button (the primary action), IconButton (the secondary, caret-only action), and Dropdown Menu (the secondary action's floating panel), preconfigured for the primary-action-with-close-alternatives use case, rather than a third independent implementation of any of them.
tierNote: Classified as a molecule, but its secondary action's dropdown panel composes Dropdown Menu (an organism, itself built from Menu + Popup) - the same deliberate, documented exception Tag Group and Avatar Group already established. See tag-group.contract.json's own tierNote for the full reasoning; not re-derived here.

sourceFiles.note: split-button.module.css contains no raw values other than 0 (squared corners - 'no radius' has no meaningful token to reference).

figmaSource.note: Correctly named in Figma - filed on the file's own "✅⏲️ Split Button" page, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin.
figmaSource.structure: 24 variants cross `tone` (default/primary - code calls this `appearance`) x `size` (xs/sm/md/lg, matching Button's own four sizes exactly) x `isDisabled` x `isOpen`, with isOpen never crossed with isDisabled=true (8 tone x size combinations x 3 states [isDisabled=false+isOpen=false, isDisabled=false+isOpen=true, isDisabled=true] = 24). Each variant is layoutMode HORIZONTAL, itemSpacing 0, containing: a real `button` (Button) instance whose trailing corners are squared to 0 (leading corners keep Button's own per-size radius - measured topLeft/bottomLeft: 12, topRight/bottomRight: 0 at size=lg) AND whose trailing-edge stroke is individually zeroed (measured strokeTopWeight/strokeBottomWeight/strokeLeftWeight: 1, strokeRightWeight: 0); a `figma-parts / split-button / divider` instance (a single 1px VECTOR, height matching the button, fill color keyed to tone); and a `popup` instance (alignment="bottom right") whose trigger slot holds a `figma-parts / secondary-action` instance - traced one level deeper, a real `icon-button` (IconButton) instance (shape=square) with a single `caret_down` icon child, whose leading corners are squared to 0 (trailing corners keep IconButton's own radius, the exact mirror of the primary action) AND whose leading-edge stroke is individually zeroed (measured strokeLeftWeight: 0, the exact mirror of the primary action's strokeRightWeight: 0). The popup's own surface slot holds the generic `figma-parts/panelSurface` with an empty content slot in the static file (isOpen=false examples) or also empty even where isOpen=true (same 'static mockup, real content is a code decision' pattern as Tag Group/Avatar Group's own dropdown-menu instances).
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's own reference instance for the open panel is a raw `popup` instance, not a `dropdown-menu` instance - but the panel's real purpose ("choose from a small group of similar actions", per the component's own Figma description) is exactly Dropdown Menu's established use case. Code reuses Dropdown Menu directly (children=the secondary-action IconButton, sections=the small group of actions) rather than hand-assembling Popup and Menu a second time, matching Tag Group/Avatar Group's own precedent rather than literally mirroring this one instance's authoring shortcut.

appearance is deliberately narrower than Button's own (`'default' | 'primary'` only, omitting `'subtle'`) - every one of the 24 verified split-button variants uses only default/primary; Figma never shows a subtle split button, so code doesn't invent one.

secondaryActionLabel is a required prop, not auto-derived from the primary action's own label - the caret segment has no visible text to derive a name from, and an auto-generated label (e.g. `${children} options`) could read oddly for non-string labels.

The figma-parts / split-button / divider part is not implemented as a new exported primitive - it's namespaced as component-specific in Figma (unlike figma-parts / secondary-action, which is reused across other components), and no existing shared Divider component exists in this codebase to reuse instead. Implemented as a single internal <span>.

IconButton's own isExpanded prop is not passed to the secondary action - verified directly in code that it only sets aria-expanded/data-expanded with no corresponding CSS (no visual effect today), and Popup (via Dropdown Menu) already overwrites aria-expanded via its own trigger-cloning regardless of whatever IconButton would set internally.

Verified directly that IconButton's own tooltip-auto-wrapping (triggered by passing an explicit aria-label, IconButton's own pre-existing behavior unrelated to Split Button) does not interfere with the outer Popup's (Dropdown Menu's) own trigger-cloning - ref and aria-expanded/aria-controls are injected as props on the authored <IconButton> element itself and correctly routed to its real internal <button> via IconButton's own forwardRef and prop-destructuring, regardless of what IconButton renders around it internally. This exact combination already exists, unremarked, in Dropdown Menu's own Content story.

alignment is hardcoded to 'right' on the internal DropdownMenu call, not exposed as a SplitButtonProps prop - Figma's own split-button variant set has no alignment axis at all; every one of the 24 variants opens "bottom right". This is a preferred alignment only, not a forced one - it maps to Popup's own 'bottomRight' (via Dropdown Menu's ALIGNMENT_MAP), and Popup's own collision detection already flips to an alternate alignment (then clamps to the viewport) when there isn't room, with no extra logic needed in Split Button.
isFullWidth is omitted from the Button props Split Button inherits (Omit<ButtonProps, 'appearance' | 'isFullWidth'>) - no verified Figma variant for a full-width split button exists.

Each segment suppresses its own border on the interior edge (border-inline-end-width: 0 on .primaryAction, border-inline-start-width: 0 on .secondaryAction) - Figma's own button/icon-button instances measure strokeRightWeight/strokeLeftWeight: 0 on that exact edge, so the divider is the only thing drawing that seam. Caught live in Storybook: without this, Button's/IconButton's own 1px border on that edge stacked with the 1px divider into a visibly wide line instead of one clean 1px seam.

IconButton's own appearance_primary:disabled (and appearance_subtle:disabled) was fixed to stay borderless (border-color: transparent), matching Button's own disabled rule split and Figma's own disabled variants (identical fill regardless of tone, but primary/subtle drop the stroke entirely - verified directly against Figma's disabled component variants). It previously shared the same visible-border rule as appearance_default:disabled, so a disabled primary secondary action looked identical to a disabled default one. This is an IconButton-atom fix (icon-button.module.css), not Split-Button-specific, but Split Button's primary+disabled secondary action is what surfaced it.

The primary-appearance divider's fill is bound to a Figma variable named color/border/brand/primary/subtle. That variable name has no code-side counterpart, and neither does its obvious-looking non-subtle sibling color-border-brand-primary actually work here - it resolves to the same prussian-900 primitive as the primary button's own background (color-background-brand-primary-bold-default), so a divider painted in it disappears against an identical-colored surface. Resolving Figma's fill node directly (not just the variable name) gives prussian-300, a light tint, not a darker/duller shade of prussian-900. No color-border-* token exists at that step, but color-content-brand-primary-subtle already aliases exactly prussian-300 - reused here on a background-color the same way Slider's own active track-stop dot already reuses it for contrast against a bold fill (see slider.module.css's own comment). Caught live in Storybook twice: first the mistyped -subtle name resolved to nothing (fully transparent); after that fix, the syntactically-valid color-border-brand-primary substitute was present but exactly camouflaged against both buttons' own background.

useCases: A primary action with a small number of closely related alternatives (Save / Save as... / Save a copy)
A primary action paired with alternate framings of the same task (Send for signature / Send as draft / Preview before sending)
antiPatterns: A single action with no alternatives - use Button directly
An icon-only trigger with no separate primary action - compose Icon Button with Dropdown Menu directly
More than a small group of similar actions, or actions unrelated to the primary one - use Dropdown Menu on its own, or Button Group

anatomy.name: primary action
anatomy.description: A real Button with every one of its own props forwarded, except appearance (narrowed) and isFullWidth (unsupported). Trailing corners squared to 0.

anatomy.name: divider
anatomy.description: A 1px internal <span>, not its own exported component. Height matches the button height per size; color keyed to appearance, overridden when disabled.

anatomy.name: secondary action
anatomy.description: A real IconButton (shape="square") showing a caret, wrapped in a DropdownMenu. Leading corners squared to 0. Accessible name and tooltip both come from secondaryActionLabel.

anatomy.name: panel
anatomy.description: Dropdown Menu's Menu, rendering the given sections - the small group of related actions.

children.description: The primary action's own label, forwarded to Button as its own children.

sections.description: The small group of related actions shown when the secondary segment opens.

secondaryActionLabel.description: Accessible name (and tooltip) for the secondary segment and its panel.

appearance.description: Applied to both segments. Narrower than Button's own appearance - no 'subtle', matching every verified Figma variant.

isLoading.description: Applies Button's own loading treatment to the primary action only; also disables the secondary action.

onClick.description: The primary action's own click handler.

tone.description: Forwarded to the primary action, unchanged from Button's own prop.

iconBefore.description: Forwarded to the primary action, unchanged from Button's own prop.

iconAfter.description: Forwarded to the primary action, unchanged from Button's own prop.

className.description: Composes with the root element's class list.

default.purpose: Neutral visual weight - matches Figma's own default.

accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the secondary action by Popup (via Dropdown Menu), reflecting the panel's open state
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the secondary action by Popup, pointing at the panel id while open
accessibility.panelRole: menu (set by Menu, via Dropdown Menu), named by secondaryActionLabel
accessibility.loadingBehavior: aria-busy/aria-disabled on the primary action (Button's own existing behavior) - not native disabled, so it stays focusable

keyboardInteraction: Tab moves between the primary action and the secondary action, in DOM order
Enter/Space activates either segment (native button behavior)
Escape closes the open panel (inherited from Popup, via Dropdown Menu)
Arrow keys/Home/End/Enter navigate and activate rows inside the open panel (inherited from Menu)
behaviorRules: Holds exactly one piece of state (open) to drive the secondary action's DropdownMenu, which is itself fully controlled.
disabled disables both segments together (native disabled on both).
isLoading applies only to the primary action (Button's own loading treatment) but additionally sets the secondary action's own disabled to disabled || isLoading.
appearance and size are applied uniformly to both segments - there is no per-segment mixing in Figma's own variant set.
showSearch is hardcoded to false and alignment to 'right' on the internal DropdownMenu - neither is exposed as a SplitButtonProps prop.
Does not pass isExpanded to the secondary action's IconButton - redundant, since Popup already manages aria-expanded via trigger-cloning.
compositionRules: Pass every other Button prop (tone, iconBefore, iconAfter, any native button attribute) directly on SplitButtonProps - they forward straight to the primary action via {...rest}.
Provide secondaryActionLabel explicitly - it is not derived from children.
Provide sections for the small group of related actions - Split Button does not accept arbitrary panel content, matching Dropdown Menu's own 'always renders a Menu' rule.
responsiveRules: The root hugs its own content width at any container size, identical to a plain inline-flex layout.
The panel inherits Popup's resize/scroll-driven repositioning and touch-friendly outside-dismissal identically to Dropdown Menu.
themeRules: Inherits Button's, IconButton's, and Dropdown Menu/Menu's token-driven theming - no component-level light/dark branching of its own.

tokens.note: split-button.module.css declares no raw values other than 0 (squared corners). The divider uses border-width-sm, size-control-xs/sm/md/lg, color-border-input/color-content-brand-primary-subtle/color-border-disabled. Every other value is Button's, IconButton's, or Dropdown Menu/Menu's own tokens - see their respective contract.json files.

do: Pass every other Button prop directly on SplitButtonProps rather than constructing a separate Button element.
Provide a specific, real secondaryActionLabel (e.g. "More Save options"), not a generic placeholder.
dont: Do not expect a 'subtle' appearance - only 'default' and 'primary' are supported.
Do not expect the secondary action to derive its own accessible name automatically - secondaryActionLabel is required.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders the primary action with its own label and the secondary action with secondaryActionLabel as its accessible name.
Activating the secondary action opens a role="menu" panel listing every item from sections, named by secondaryActionLabel.
Selecting a panel item calls that item's own onSelect - Split Button does not intercept or assume anything about the selection.
disabled disables both segments (native disabled on both); isLoading applies Button's own loading treatment to the primary action and also disables the secondary action.
Applies appearance and size uniformly to both segments.
Forwards a ref to the primary action's underlying button element.
Supports a custom id/className on the root.
knownLimitations: No built-in support for more than a small, static list of actions - very large sections arrays inherit Menu's own eager-rendering behavior (no virtualization).
Inherits every one of Dropdown Menu's and Menu's own knownLimitations for the panel (no typeahead, no built-in focus-first-item-on-open).
futureEnhancements: A renderSecondaryAction/custom-icon escape hatch, if a real use case needs something other than the caret.
Exposing alignment, if a real layout ever needs the panel to open left instead of right.
